input.strategy_title: Audit logging for model inference traffic
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Financial-services customers cannot pass compliance reviews because inference
traffic on RHOAI leaves no audit trail: there is no record of who invoked which
model endpoint, when, and with what outcome. Auditors require tamper-evident,
structured audit events for every inference request. Without this, two
strategic renewals are at risk this fiscal year.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Every inference request through a KServe endpoint emits an audit event capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status (not payloads). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Audit events are delivered to the cluster audit sink with at-least-once semantics and are not lost on component restart. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Administrators can enable/disable inference auditing per project from the Dashboard. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | A common audit event schema is defined and published so future components (pipelines, workbenches) emit compatible events. Note: the schema in this item is the format HLR-1's events must conform to — HLR-1 cannot ship before the schema is settled. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Documentation covers enabling auditing and interpreting events. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- Auditing of non-inference traffic (pipeline runs, notebook activity) — future
  strategies will adopt the HLR-4 schema
- Long-term audit storage and retention tooling (customer-provided)

## Open Questions

None — the audit sink interface is the standard cluster logging forwarder.

# Define and publish the common inference audit event schema

## Description

This epic defines the structured audit event schema that every inference audit
event must conform to, and publishes it as the shared contract for the platform.
It is the foundation the inference audit emission capability builds against, and
it is the format future components (pipelines, workbenches) will adopt so their
audit events are compatible. The schema exists to satisfy financial-services
compliance requirements: auditors need structured, tamper-evident records of who
invoked which model endpoint, when, and with what outcome.

## Scope

- Define the common audit event schema, including fields for:
  - caller identity
  - model and version
  - timestamp
  - response status
- Explicitly exclude request and response payloads from the schema — audit
  events record metadata about the request, never the content
- Publish and version the schema in a location where future platform components
  (pipelines, workbenches) can find it and emit compatible events without
  ad-hoc coordination
- Ensure the schema's structure is deliverable through the cluster audit sink
  (the standard cluster logging forwarder interface)

## Acceptance Criteria

- The schema defines fields covering caller identity, model/version, timestamp,
  and response status
- The schema contains no field for request/response payload content, and the
  exclusion is documented as a compliance requirement
- The schema is published and versioned; a component author with no prior
  context can locate it and construct a conforming event
- The schema structure has been reviewed for compatibility with ingestion by the
  standard cluster logging forwarder

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2) — a common audit event schema is defined and published so future
  components emit compatible events. Priority raised to P0 by inheritance: the
  strategy states the inference audit emission requirement (HLR-1, P0) cannot
  ship before this schema is settled.

# Emit inference audit events from KServe with reliable delivery to the cluster audit sink

## Description

This epic implements the core compliance capability: every inference request
through a KServe endpoint emits a structured audit event — capturing caller
identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status (never payloads) — and
the event is delivered to the cluster audit sink with at-least-once semantics
that survive component restarts. Events conform to the published common audit
event schema so they are interpretable by auditors and compatible with future
components' events.

## Scope

- Emit an audit event on the KServe inference request path for every inference
  request, capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response
  status; no request or response payload content is captured
- Conform all emitted events to the published common audit event schema
- Deliver events to the cluster audit sink (the standard cluster logging
  forwarder) with at-least-once semantics
- Buffer and retry delivery so events are not lost when the emitting component
  restarts
- Provide a per-project audit enablement configuration that the serving stack
  honors (auditing on/off per project) — this is the surface the Dashboard
  administration capability writes; the exact mechanism (CR field vs. config
  resource) is an implementation decision for the serving team

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every inference request through a KServe endpoint produces exactly the
  required audit event fields (caller identity, model/version, timestamp,
  response status) and no payload content
- Emitted events validate against the published common audit event schema
- Delivery to the cluster audit sink is at-least-once: a test that restarts the
  emitting component while inference traffic is flowing shows no audit event loss
- Setting the per-project audit configuration to disabled suppresses event
  emission for that project; enabled resumes emission
- The build pipeline is green on the changes

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — every inference request through a KServe endpoint emits an audit
  event capturing caller identity, model/version, timestamp, and response status
  (not payloads)
- HLR-2 (P0) — audit events are delivered to the cluster audit sink with
  at-least-once semantics and are not lost on component restart

# Per-project inference auditing administration in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic gives administrators a Dashboard control to enable and disable
inference auditing per project. It is the user-facing administration surface for
the inference audit capability: the Dashboard reads and writes the per-project
audit configuration through the Kubernetes API, following its existing
configuration and feature-flag integration patterns, and the serving stack
honors the setting.

## Scope

- Add an administration control in the Dashboard to enable/disable inference
  auditing for a data science project
- Read and write the per-project audit configuration via the Kubernetes API,
  consistent with the Dashboard's existing per-component feature-flag and
  config-CR patterns (the Dashboard owns no data plane)
- Surface the current auditing state per project so administrators can verify
  the setting
- Restrict the control to administrator-appropriate access, consistent with
  existing Dashboard permission patterns

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable and disable inference auditing for a specific
  project from the Dashboard
- The setting takes effect on the serving side: audit events are emitted for
  the project when enabled and suppressed when disabled
- The Dashboard displays the current per-project auditing state accurately
- The control is not exposed to users without administrator-level project
  access, consistent with existing Dashboard permission behavior
- The build pipeline is green on the changes

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1) — administrators can enable/disable inference auditing per project
  from the Dashboard

# Document enabling inference auditing and interpreting audit events

## Description

This epic produces the customer-facing documentation for inference auditing:
how to enable it (cluster-level and per project through the Dashboard
administration control) and how to interpret the audit events it produces. The
documentation describes the capability as built and is technically reviewed
against the implementation.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Enabling inference auditing
  - Prerequisites and cluster audit sink (standard cluster logging forwarder)
    configuration
  - Enabling/disabling auditing per project from the Dashboard administration
    control
- Interpreting audit events
  - The common audit event schema: caller identity, model/version, timestamp,
    response status — and the explicit absence of payload content
  - At-least-once delivery semantics and what that means for audit review
    (possible duplicates, never lost on restart)
- Verifying the audit trail — how to confirm events are arriving at the sink
  and how to read them back for a compliance review

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers enabling inference auditing, including the
  per-project Dashboard toggle, and interpreting audit events against the
  published schema
- The documentation includes a verification procedure an administrator can
  follow to confirm audit events are being delivered
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented capability by the
  owning engineers before publication
- The documentation is published through the Red Hat docs content process

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2) — documentation covers enabling auditing and interpreting events
